title: Model management per role: one audited change, caps, and a stronger model only when it measured better
request: Each role's model chosen per role with a reviewer and a reason, prompts versioned, spend caps per role, a page showing each role's model, prompt version, score and cost; a stronger model for the understanding roles only when it measures better on the conversations. Switching a role's model must be one audited change, and the conversation suite must report each role's score and cost by model.
spec: Routing changes and their audit row in one call; per-purpose caps in the gateway; the measured-better rule in routing; conversation runs that name their roles' models, prompts and costs; one page per role.
plan: Map what exists: routing by tier, the shadow log, caps, the Admin table, the conversation suite.
Make the change and its audit one call, with the model, prompt version and measurement.
Add per-role caps and enforce them in the gateway.
Record each role's model and cost in conversation runs; compare models only on the same conversations.
Show each role on one page.

decisions.decision: A role's model stays its tier's model; a move is a move to another tier.
decisions.why: Per-role model strings would bypass the tier's approved endpoint and key; the tier is already the unit a reviewer approves.

decisions.decision: The bar for a stronger model is its own tier's model and the approved one, never the tier it stands on now.
decisions.why: Measured against where it stands, a step down and up again would bring a worse model in.

decisions.decision: Each model's score is its mean over all runs on the same conversations.
decisions.why: With the newest run only, a rerun could pick its luck.

decisions.decision: The prompt version is a content hash.
decisions.why: The prompts already carry pinned hashes; a number would need its own bookkeeping and could drift from the text.

change: dclab_rnd/models/routing.py, gateway.py, usage.py, overview.py (new), agentic/routers/core.py, agentic/api_models.py, agent_eval/conversation, core_advisor.py, the Admin page (views/admin.html, features.js; the built app and api.js regenerated); tests/test_model_management.py (new); the plan, the roadmap, CLAUDE.md.

findings.defect: Moving a role back to its own tier lost the target in the audit.
findings.scenario: The audit row of a move back had no to field.
findings.cause: Empty values were dropped from the row.
findings.fix: The four core fields are always written; only the extras are dropped when empty.

findings.defect: The same change again wrote a second audit row.
findings.scenario: Serving a role with the tier it already had was recorded as a change.
findings.cause: An edit removed the early return for an unchanged setting.

findings.defect: A step down and up again brought a worse model in.
findings.scenario: Refused on strong, moved to cheap, then strong was compared with the cheap model and allowed.
findings.cause: The bar was the tier serving the role now.
findings.fix: The bar is its own tier's model and the approved one.

findings.defect: The tuned tier needed no measurement.
findings.scenario: An understanding role moved to a tuned tier configured as any model.
findings.cause: Only a higher-ranked tier counted as stronger.
findings.fix: Every move but one to a weaker tier needs the measurement.

findings.defect: Models measured on different conversations were compared.
findings.scenario: A run on nine dev conversations against one on twelve, both called dev.
findings.cause: Runs were grouped by split name only.
findings.fix: Each run stores the conversations' fingerprint; models compare only on the same one.

findings.defect: The newest run of each model was its score.
findings.scenario: Rerunning a model until the noise favoured it would decide the move.
findings.fix: The mean over all its runs on the same conversations.

findings.defect: Three understanding roles can never pass the measured path.
findings.scenario: The conversation suite asks only the reader.
findings.cause: The other roles have their own suites, not tied to a model.
findings.fix: Stated in the plan's status and on the page; the owner's override, audited, is their path.

findings.defect: A cap that is not a number was accepted.
findings.scenario: A NaN cap capped nothing while the audit said a cap was set.
findings.fix: A cap is a finite number, zero or more.

findings.defect: A model changed in the environment bypasses the rule, and a cap cannot stop an unpriced model.
findings.scenario: A stronger model set in .env serves a tier with no review; an unpriced model's spend never reaches a cap.
findings.cause: Approval pins routed tiers only; caps count euros.
findings.fix: Said on the page, in the cap dialog and in the plan.

outcome: A role's model, shadow or cap changes in one audited call naming the model, prompt version and measurement; caps per role stop spending; an understanding role gets another model only when it measured better on the same conversations; one page shows it all.
lessons: A rule that compares with the current state can be walked around one step at a time: compare with a fixed bar.
A measurement is comparable only on the same items: fingerprint the set.
When a replacement block spans several statements, check that none of the lines between was lost.
risks: Only the conversation reader is measured by model today.
An unpriced model escapes euro caps.
